approach: Velocity is the slope of the s-t graph, and its direction reverses only where the slope changes sign, not where the curve's concavity changes.

steps.text: Recall what the slope of the s-t graph represents.
Point A is an inflection point, where the curve changes from concave upward to concave downward, meaning the rate of change of slope changes sign, not the slope itself.
Since the displacement keeps rising from 0 through A to B, the slope stays positive throughout, so the velocity does not change direction at A.
The Reason, that the sign of the slope decides the direction of velocity, is a true general statement, but it does not make the Assertion true here.

final_answer.value: Assertion is false but the Reason is true.
